### When is the best time to buy tech products?
The best deals typically appear during Black Friday (November), Prime Day (July), and post-holiday sales (January). New product launches in September-October often trigger discounts on previous generation models.

### For the discounted RDNA 4 (or equivalent future architecture) graphics cards featured in the January 2026 deals, what specific architectural improvements have been implemented in their Ray Tracing Units (RTUs) that significantly enhance hardware-accelerated global illumination and real-time path tracing, beyond simple BVH traversal optimization?
The RDNA 4 series introduces enhanced 2nd-gen RTUs with a dedicated asynchronous shader architecture for improved ray-box and ray-triangle intersection throughput. This results in an average 35-40% uplift in complex global illumination scenes and enables more efficient denoising filters with less performance overhead compared to RDNA 3, moving beyond just simple bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) optimizations to better handle diffuse and specular reflections concurrently.

### Regarding the premium QD-OLED display deals, specifically the new 49-inch ultrawide models, what is the actual subpixel arrangement (e.g., RGB triangular vs. WRGB with white subpixel) and how does this impact effective pixel density and text rendering clarity when compared to a traditional 49-inch 5120x1440 IPS panel, especially for productivity tasks requiring sharp small fonts?
The featured QD-OLED ultrawides typically utilize a true RGB triangular subpixel arrangement, which provides superior color purity and eliminates the need for a white subpixel that can dilute colors or cause color fringing. While this arrangement can sometimes lead to minor text fringing with specific anti-aliasing methods due to non-standard pixel geometry, its higher contrast and color volume generally result in a more vibrant and less fatiguing experience than IPS for mixed use. However, for extreme text clarity on very small fonts, a traditional IPS panel with a true RGB stripe can still offer slightly better subpixel rendering compatibility with Windows ClearType.

### Given the prevalence of Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) mesh systems in the latest deals, how do the advanced Multi-Link Operation (MLO) capabilities, specifically utilizing both the 5 GHz and 6 GHz bands concurrently, translate into real-world latency reductions and throughput stability for latency-sensitive applications like cloud gaming or VR streaming, particularly in environments with high spectral congestion?
Wi-Fi 7's MLO allows for simultaneous transmission and reception across multiple bands (e.g., 5 GHz and 6 GHz), effectively creating a wider data pipe and offering path redundancy. For cloud gaming and VR streaming, this significantly reduces latency spikes by enabling dynamic load balancing and quick failover between links in congested environments. The aggregated bandwidth ensures more consistent throughput, and the ability to choose the least congested path minimizes interference from neighboring networks, resulting in up to a 70% reduction in average latency variability compared to Wi-Fi 6E in high-density scenarios.
